_doc: Differential oracle for the advanced elliptic-curve modules:
Argument convention: p = 0 means QQ, otherwise GF(p). Curves are given by
an a-invariant list of length 2 ([a4, a6]) or 5 ([a1, a2, a3, a4, a6]).
The inputs are deliberately structured rather than randomly sampled: every
curve/kernel pair below was picked to hit a boundary (characteristic 2,
characteristic 3, characteristic dividing the isogeny degree, even Kohel
degree, j = 0, j = 1728, supersingular, long Weierstrass with a1 and a3
non-zero, non-fundamental and non-discriminant CM inputs, degenerate class
numbers). Small dense random curves would never produce these shapes.

cases._replaced: This slot used to hold the characteristic-2 Kohel case; the port HANGS on it, so a different (running) case took its place. See _replaced_reason.
_replaced_reason: y-coordinate of the 2-torsion point, and find_sqrt (ell_curve_isogeny.ts:3324-3329)
searches for a quadratic non-residue z with z^((p-1)/2) != 1. Over GF(2) the exponent
is 0, so z^0 == 1 for every z and the loop alternates z = 0, 1, 0, 1, ... forever,
allocating a field element per iteration (observed: 6 GB RSS before the runner was
killed). SageMath returns (2, (1, 0, 0, 1, 0)) for this input.
Restore fixedValue(2) / fixedValue([1, 0, 0, 0, 1]) / fixedValue([0, 1]) here, and in
handles characteristic 2 (where every element is a square and sqrt(a) = a^(q/2)).
It is kept here rather than deleted because a hanging case makes the WHOLE area
un-runnable -- compare.ts would never get a transcript for any other case either.
